overloadMerges.note: The two doc syntax lines differ only in whether the leading '*' is passed (selecting whether object is a name-string vs. a Variable/Field reference); collapsed into one overload with an optional literal-symbol discriminator.

params.name: asObjectName
params.description: If specified, Object is an Object Name (String); if omitted, Object is a Field, Variable, or Table.

params.name: object
params.description: Object Name (if * is specified), or Variable or Field or Table (if * is omitted)

params.name: enterable
params.description: Boolean: True=enterable, False=non-enterable. Longint: 0=not enterable, 1=enterable, 2=not enterable and not focusable.

sentinelValues.meaning: obk enterable -- object is enterable and focusable
obk not enterable -- object is not enterable, but an input/4D Write Pro area remains focusable
obk not enterable not focusable -- object is not enterable and an input/4D Write Pro area is not focusable

overloadMerges.semanticRole: Makes the form object(s) designated by object and * enterable or non-enterable, and (via a Longint value) can additionally control whether a non-enterable input or 4D Write Pro area remains focusable.

constraints: Boolean False behaves differently by database kind: in binary databases the focusable attribute then follows the object's Focusable property; in projects the object remains focusable regardless.

Can enable 'Enter in List' mode for subforms/list forms used with MODIFY SELECTION/DISPLAY SELECTION: for subforms pass the subform table name or subform object name (from the subform's own form method); for list forms pass the list form's table.
Making an object non-enterable does not prevent changing its value programmatically.
To make a single list box cell non-enterable, pass -1 to $0 in the On Before Data Entry event instead of using this command.
